executive_summary: Day-30 checkpoint on Priority Recommendations shows no detectable aggregate effect: recommendation_engagement_rate is 0.5662% treatment vs control, below the 1.2% minimum detectable effect. That aggregate is misleading. iOS/DE treatment users show a -8.3766% decline in recommendation_engagement_rate with no equivalent movement in the control arm, which is consistent with a genuine feature effect in that market and may be offsetting gains elsewhere. Instrumentation is healthy across all events, so this is unlikely to be a measurement artefact. Escalating for a human decision on whether to hold the German iOS rollout.

segment_findings.observation: recommendation_engagement_rate in iOS/DE moved -8.3766% over the window, accounting for 38.9% of total absolute movement. The treatment arm moved -16.4961% against -0.3069% in control.
segment_findings.limitations: Single market and platform; no qualitative signal on why German users respond differently. Sub-segment cell sizes below the market level are not examined.

facts.statement: Aggregate recommendation_engagement_rate is 0.5662% treatment vs control, below the 1.2% minimum detectable effect.
recommendation_engagement_rate in iOS/DE fell 8.3766% over the window, with the movement confined to the treatment arm.
Every critical event is above the 95% completeness floor in all eligible markets, so no metric in this checkpoint is compromised by measurement.
day7_retention_proxy is 0.1861% treatment vs control in aggregate and within its guardrail threshold.

hypotheses.statement: Priority Recommendations may suppress engaged recommendations for German iOS users, possibly through recommendation ranking that suits the local catalogue depth poorly.
hypotheses.how_to_test: Compare recommendation engagement rate by recipient bucket within iOS/DE treatment against iOS/US treatment; if ranking is the mechanism, acceptance should differ.

hypotheses.statement: The iOS/DE movement could be a market-specific seasonal or competitive effect unrelated to the feature.
hypotheses.how_to_test: An external effect would move the control arm too. Control moved -0.3069%, which argues against this.

recommended_actions.action: Hold the German iOS rollout at its current share pending a ranking review.
recommended_actions.rationale: A treatment-only decline of this size in one market is worth pausing on, and the aggregate does not justify expanding.

recommended_actions.action: Run the intro acceptance comparison for iOS/DE against iOS/US within treatment.
recommended_actions.rationale: Cheapest test that separates a ranking mechanism from a market effect.

escalation_reasons: Aggregate primary outcome does not clear the 1.2% minimum detectable effect.
A treatment-only decline in iOS/DE requires a product decision on the German rollout.
